What is the horizontal component of the force shown?
20 N
53
horizontal
A
12 N
B
16 N
C
25 N
D
27 N

hints: Notice the $20 \text{ N}$ arrow makes $53^\circ$ with the dashed horizontal line, so the horizontal side is adjacent to the angle.
Recall the adjacent component uses cosine: horizontal $= F \cos \theta$ and vertical $= F \sin \theta$.
Use $\cos 53^\circ \approx 0.6$ to evaluate $20 \cos 53^\circ$ and check that the result must be less than $20 \text{ N}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given vector: magnitude $F = 20 \text{ N}$ at $\theta = 53^\circ$ above the horizontal dashed line.
State the component rule: the component adjacent to the angle is $F \cos \theta$, so horizontal component $= 20 \cos 53^\circ$.
Check units and sense: the result is in $\text{N}$ and $12 \text{ N}$ is less than $20 \text{ N}$, as a component must be.

B.explanation: This is the vertical component $20 \sin 53^\circ \approx 16 \text{ N}$, not the horizontal component.

C.explanation: A component cannot be larger than the $20 \text{ N}$ magnitude, so $25 \text{ N}$ is impossible.

D.explanation: A component cannot be larger than the $20 \text{ N}$ magnitude, so $27 \text{ N}$ is impossible.
